names.why: Company press release of 2026-11-18 (PR Newswire, seen via Finviz https://finviz.com/news/424443/x-financial-to-report-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-on-november-27-2026) sets Q3 2026 results before the US open on Fri 2026-11-27, so the calendar row is right. Two caveats. First, the baseline's reaction history is not an earnings history: the cadence check itself flags it, and the 2026-11-06 +22.34% is the going-private proposal, not a print. Second, the stock now trades as a non-binding take-private at US$6.03/ADS from the 93.45%-voting controlling shareholder, so the reaction to the print is bounded by the deal spread (spot 5.25 vs 6.03, about 15%). The reaction lands in a thin 13:00 ET half-day session.
names.session_evidence: Company release: results 'before the open of U.S. markets on Friday, November 27, 2026', call 08:00 ET / 21:00 Beijing (https://finviz.com/news/424443/x-financial-to-report-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-on-november-27-2026). So bmo, and the reaction falls in the 2026-11-27 half-day session.
where_to_look: The going-private track. Look for any special-committee formation, financial-advisor hire, financing commitment, or a revised or withdrawn proposal from Mangrove Coast, in 6-Ks or the Schedule 13D/A at https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001725033. The Q3 release may carry a deal-status paragraph. The deal spread and its probability matter more than the quarter. (proposal: https://www.panabee.com/news/x-financial-receives-going-private-proposal-from-controlling-shareholder ; https://www.bbtnews.com.cn/2026/1106/610644.shtml)

Whether the Q3 numbers or Q4 guidance could anchor or undercut the $6.03 price. Book value per ADS against the offer. Q2 2026 net revenue fell 56.3% YoY and loan volume fell 70.2% YoY (https://finviz.com/news/384651/x-financial-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results), so the trajectory of loan facilitation volume and of 31-90 day delinquency is the swing line.

PBOC/NFRA consumer-lending rules in Q3-Q4 2026: loan pricing caps (24% APR) and the guarantee/credit-enhancement rules that hit Chinese online lenders. Read-through from peers that report before 11-27: Qifu (QFIN), FinVolution (FINV), LexinFintech (LX), Jiayin (JFIN), including their Q4 volume guides.
Capital return: whether the semi-annual dividend or the buyback continues or is suspended pending the take-private.
